back: Meeting the needs of the present without compromising the ability of future generations to meet their own needs.

front: Four stages where designers consider sustainability
back: Material choice, manufacturing process, product life and end of life.
Use fewer materials or less material, and reduce energy use.
Design the product or its components to be used again.
Use materials that can be recycled at the end of the product's life.
Design the product to be easily serviced and fixed.
Ask whether there is a fundamentally better or greener way to solve the problem.
Avoid harmful or unsustainable materials altogether.
A method of evaluating a product's total environmental impact from cradle to grave — from raw material extraction to final disposal.
1. Raw material extraction. 2. Manufacturing. 3. Use. 4. Disposal.
To find which stage of a product's life has the greatest environmental impact, so improvements can be targeted.
Designing a product so all its materials can be recovered and used again in a new product, instead of ending as waste (cradle to grave).
Deliberately designing a product with a limited useful life so consumers need to buy a replacement.
For manufacturers: repeat sales and funding for research and development. Against: more waste, higher costs for users and a throwaway culture.
Phones with batteries that cannot be replaced or updates that slow older devices; fast fashion that falls apart; printer cartridges that run out quickly.
When newer technology replaces a product even though it still works, e.g. DVD players replaced by streaming, film cameras by digital cameras.
The total amount of greenhouse gases, particularly CO₂, produced directly and indirectly by a product, organisation or person.

front: Stages that add to a product's carbon footprint
back: Raw materials, manufacturing, distribution, use and disposal.

front: Ways to reduce a product's carbon footprint
back: Source materials locally, use renewable energy in manufacturing, make products lighter, design for longevity and use recycled materials.
